scope: Additive international follow-through to the 54-record first pass. Canada, Australia, EU and India selected to test specific gaps, not a representative global sample. Worldwide history and other countries remain in the earlier research.

findings.title: Facebook expressly linked restoring news to negotiated government changes
findings.finding: Facebook's 22 February 2021 Pacific-time update, corresponding to 23 February in Australia, says discussions with Treasurer Frydenberg and Minister Fletcher produced changes addressing its concerns, enabling restoration of news and further journalism investment. Fletcher later publicly confirmed intense negotiations with Mark Zuckerberg before restoration and passage.
findings.evidence_level: Company attribution, corroborated as to negotiations by a participating minister
findings.money_status: No price for the political negotiation or precise publisher payment disclosed
findings.limit: Demonstrates acknowledged bargaining and commercial pressure, not bribery. The company describes its own success; the minister describes the government's success. This source pair does not allocate authorship of each amendment. This is platform-news policy, not AI-model legislation.

findings.title: Primary AI Act request and later provision: GitHub open-source exemption
findings.finding: GitHub's dated position paper asks to expand the research/development exemption to shared open-source code and models, and proposes scope language protecting open-source AI before deployment while retaining high-risk coverage. The Commission's later official text shows Article 2(8) excluding pre-market research/development, and Article 2(12) exempting free/open-source AI systems except high-risk systems and those under Articles 5 or 50. This is a concrete documented request followed by a partly corresponding legal provision, not an attributed causal finding.
findings.money_status: No fee, donation or payment attached to this clause was established; do not connect it to EU11/EU12 bands.
findings.limit: Reverse check: the paper itself builds on a Parliament Legal Affairs Committee report dated 12 September 2022 and text considered by Axel Voss. Thus the proposal history predates GitHub's 20 October paper; GitHub cannot be labelled the originator from this evidence. No primary legislative statement was found crediting GitHub as the cause of adoption. The Commission service page identifies its legal text as consolidated at 27 July 2026; it is not a frozen 2024 page.

findings.title: Treasury attributed commercial deals to regulatory pressure but could not audit their prices
findings.finding: Australia's Treasury review concluded that over 30 Google/Meta agreements were unlikely without the code. It also stated that parties had not supplied the confidential agreements. Its reference to more than A$200m came from Rod Sims's estimate, not a transaction audit. The report names recipients and documents differing outcomes, including publishers unable to secure deals.
findings.evidence_level: Government evaluation with explicit access and measurement limits
findings.money_status: A$200m-plus is an attributed estimate; no verified aggregate disbursement established here
findings.limit: A declared estimate must not be converted into exact paid cash. Treasury's counterfactual assessment is an evaluative conclusion rather than an experimental causal estimate. The code incentivized private deals, so statutory adoption and actual receipt are separate questions.

findings.title: The draft exemption threshold was a revenue proxy, not a fixed C$172 million statutory bill
findings.finding: The Online News Act received royal assent on June 22, 2023; its main application and bargaining provisions commenced December 19. Sections 11 and 84 establish exemption criteria and regulation-making authority. The September 2 draft proposed a sustainability threshold: relevant intermediary global revenue × Canada's share of global GDP (approximately 2%) × 4%. Unrelated company revenue was excluded. This was an exemption criterion for negotiated agreements, not 4% of all Alphabet revenue or a fixed amount written into the Act.
findings.evidence_level: Primary statute and proposed regulation with explanatory statement
findings.money_status: Proposed threshold; neither an assessed tax nor a verified payment
findings.limit: The reviewed draft does not state C$172 million. Exact application would require the relevant revenue, GDP inputs and valuation period; no reconstruction from guessed inputs is presented.

findings.finding: In the November 29 Senate debate, Senator Julie Miville-Dechêne contrasted the C$100 million agreement with an expected C$172 million. findings.money_status: Expected amount discussed by legislators versus announced agreement; neither statement is proof of a C$172 million payment or assessment
findings.limit: No originating government model establishing the C$172 million estimate was located. Do not label the difference a forgiven debt, tax cut or verified saving. The documentary regulatory changes in CA02 stand independently of this missing model.

findings.title: Government expressly connected changes to Google's stated concerns
findings.finding: The final regulations' explanatory statement says Google objected that the draft formula created a floor without a ceiling and uncertain liability. The formula was removed; a C$100 million annually indexed provision for the largest search engine was added to secure Google's continued participation. The notification period also changed from 30 to 180 days following Google's concerns. On November 29, Minister Pascale St-Onge publicly described weeks of discussions leading to the C$100 million, single-collective arrangement. The final instrument was registered December 15, 2023 and published January 3, 2024.
findings.evidence_level: Primary final regulation, government explanation and ministerial statement
findings.money_status: Annual monetary exemption benchmark, indexed; not a political donation or payment to government
findings.limit: This documents a government-acknowledged response to corporate representations. It does not establish bribery or exclusive corporate authorship. The explanatory statement is not itself the regulation.

findings.title: The regulator imposed limits rather than granting an unconditional exemption
findings.finding: Google signed its CJC agreement June 6, 2024. The October 28 decision granted a five-year Google Search exemption, with payment due within 60 days. It capped administrative deductions at 2%, prohibited membership fees, and limited Google's indemnity claims and set-offs to the administrative allowance. The regulator rejected an uncapped indemnity because it could endanger news funding.
findings.money_status: Conditions on contribution handling and potential withholding; not evidence any indemnity was collected
findings.limit: The exemption is a specific statutory arrangement, not general immunity from Canadian law. Financial support does not establish editorial control.

findings.title: The enacted Australian charge is 2.75%, superseding earlier draft-rate headlines
findings.finding: The Charge Act commenced 27 August 2026; section3(2) sets 2.75%. The Administration Act uses a statutory revenue base and a A$250m liability threshold. Eligible publisher expenditure can offset liability at 150%, or 200% for qualifying smaller news groups, with a one-quarter-of-charge cap per group and an overall liability cap.

findings.money_status: Statutory calculation rules, not measured corporate taxes paid
findings.limit: Earlier draft rates do not describe the enacted rate. Corporate liability needs the defined revenue base, eligibility and offsets; no company's actual payment is calculated. The enactment counters an inference that major platforms invariably obtain reduced obligations.

findings.title: Counterevidence: open-source treatment is not blanket deregulation
findings.finding: Article 53(2) exempts qualifying open-source general-purpose models only from the documentation duties in paragraph 1(a) and (b); models with systemic risks cannot use that exception. Copyright-policy and public training-content-summary duties in paragraph 1(c) and (d) remain. Recital 103 distinguishes non-monetised repository sharing from monetised components. These limits prevent describing the open-source result as complete acceptance of a broad model exemption.
findings.money_status: No monetary attribution established.
findings.limit: The exact beneficiary of a legal exception requires facts about the model, licence, availability and use. A matching policy preference is not proof that spending bought the provision. The service text is the current consolidated presentation, not independently recovered historical negotiation text.
